claims.text: As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has a density of 10.21 g cm−3.
The proposed intervention is addition of 5 at.% Sc to as-cast HfMoTaTiZr.
Adding 5 at.% Sc will produce a Sc-rich phase.
The proposed Sc-rich phase will have a lower density than the original alloy or matrix.
Alloying and Sc-rich phase formation will reduce the bulk alloy density.
Adding 5 at.% Sc will reduce density by 5%, from 10.21 to 9.70 g cm−3.
The Sc-modified alloy will retain the mechanical properties of as-cast HfMoTaTiZr at room temperature.
The Sc-modified alloy will retain the mechanical properties of as-cast HfMoTaTiZr at elevated temperatures up to 1000 °C.
The stated temperature boundary is room temperature through 1000 °C.
No loading-mode, strain-rate, stress-state, or exposure-time boundary is specified.
The test will measure density, yield strength, and ultimate tensile strength at room temperature and 1000 °C for alloys with varying Sc contents.
The hypothesis will be rejected if density reduction is less than 3%.
The hypothesis will be rejected if room-temperature or 1000 °C mechanical properties decline by more than 10%.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis says mechanical properties will not be sacrificed, but the rejection rule permits reductions of up to 10% without falsification. Thus the operational criterion does not strictly test the stated no-sacrifice outcome.

The predicted density reduction is specifically 5%, whereas the hypothesis is not rejected for reductions between 3% and 5%; the rejection threshold therefore does not decisively test the quantified prediction.
